transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started. We have an administrative charge from a former employee alleging discrimination, retaliation, and failure to accommodate a religious practice. The agency has acknowledged receipt and is requesting our position statement. I understand the separation was approved under our ordinary performance-management process, and we haven't yet made a settlement proposal. Before we draft our response, I need to understand the specifics. Who can walk me through the allegations in the charge file -- particularly the supervisor's conduct, the accommodation request, and the separation decision?

My review of the last two years of discipline records found two similarly situated employees who received materially different discipline for comparable attendance conduct. I recommend we conduct an independent comparator review covering exactly three employees before we assert in our position statement that discipline was consistent. My audit worksheet is still in the HR investigations folder if anyone needs to reference it. If we assert consistency without addressing these comparators, we could be creating exposure rather than mitigating it.
